entity.summary: If you use a business name other than your own personal name, register it with the Montana Secretary of State; DLI suggests doing this before applying for your construction contractor license.
entity.quote: Should I register my business name with the Montana Secretary of State? Yes. All persons using a business name other than their personal name should register.

state_tax.summary: Montana has no general sales tax. Once you pay wages, register for a Montana withholding tax account with the Department of Revenue.
state_tax.quote: You must register for a Montana withholding tax account if you: Issue Montana wages Issue Forms W-2 (with or without withholding)

unemployment.summary: You are a covered employer who must register and pay Montana unemployment insurance tax once your annual payroll reaches $1,000 (or you meet another listed test).
unemployment.quote: Your total annual payroll for the current or preceding calendar year equals or exceeds $1,000.

workers_comp.summary: If you hire employees you must cover them under a Montana workers' compensation policy. Working alone as an independent contractor, you need either an Independent Contractor Exemption Certificate (ICEC) or self-elected workers' comp coverage.
workers_comp.quote: an independent contractor must obtain either an independent contractor exemption certificate or self-elected coverage under a Montana workers' compensation insurance policy.

local.summary: Certified local governments may enforce building and mechanical codes and issue permits in their own areas; elsewhere the state Building Codes Program does.
local.quote: Certified Local Governments may enforce the mechanical code within their jurisdictional area. All other areas fall under the State's jurisdiction.

residential_building.name: Construction Contractor License (CCL), effective January 1, 2026
residential_building.covers: Contractors who build, remodel, repair, demolish, or install roofing, siding or flooring for others, specifically those with employees, plus corporations and manager-managed LLCs regardless of employee count. Solo contractors without employees use an Independent Contractor Exemption Certificate instead.
prerequisites: Workers' compensation insurance and unemployment coverage for employees
Business name registered with the Secretary of State if not your personal name
Independent Contractor Exemption Certificate if you work alone without employees
residential_building.summary: Since January 1, 2026, Montana requires a Construction Contractor License for contractors with employees and for corporations and manager-managed LLCs. It mainly confirms you carry workers' comp and unemployment coverage; there is no trade exam. Solo operators without employees instead get an Independent Contractor Exemption Certificate.
residential_building.quote: Anyone involved in the construction, alteration, repair, moving, or demolition of structures attached to real estate. This specifically targets contractors with employees, as well as corporations and manager-managed LLCs, regardless of employee count.
residential_building.note: The CCL is a business license tied to workers' comp/UI compliance, not a competency license.

evidence.quote: In Montana, a Construction Contractor License exists MCA 37-45-101. (Effective January 1, 2026)
The licensing system enforces state laws, ensuring that contractors maintain required workers' compensation insurance and unemployment coverage for their employees.
A test is not required to qualify for the ICEC.

commercial_building.name: Construction Contractor License (CCL)
commercial_building.covers: Same license as residential: covers buildings, highways, roads, excavation and other improvements to real estate.
prerequisites: Workers' compensation insurance and unemployment coverage for employees
commercial_building.summary: Commercial contractors use the same Construction Contractor License as residential contractors.
commercial_building.quote: offers to undertake, undertakes, or submits a bid to construct, alter, repair, add to, subtract from, improve, move, wreck, or demolish for another a building, highway, road, railroad, excavation, or other structure, project, development, or improvement attached to real estate

electrical.name: Electrical Contractor license; Master / Journeyman / Residential Electrician licenses
electrical.covers: Electrical contracting businesses (a master electrician must be the responsible party) and individual electricians, who must work for a licensed electrical contractor.
prerequisites: Master electrician as responsible party
Proof of workers' comp and UI compliance, or an Independent Contractor Exemption
Journeyman: completed apprenticeship (8000 hours plus 576 hours of instruction) and exam
Master: four years of licensed journeyman experience (or EE degree path) and exam
electrical.insurance: Workers' compensation and unemployment insurance compliance (or ICEC).
electrical.summary: An electrical contractor license needs a licensed master electrician as the responsible party plus workers' comp/UI compliance. Journeymen must finish an apprenticeship and pass an exam; masters need four years as a licensed journeyman and another exam.
electrical.quote: An electrical contractor license will require a Montana licensed master electrician as the responsible party and allows the electrical contractor to perform residential, commercial, industrial, and institutional work.

evidence.quote: Proof of compliance with Montana Workers Compensation and also Unemployment Insurance or an Independent Contractor Exemption .

Journeyman Electrical Apprenticeship completion is required; journeyman apprenticeship completion includes 8000 hours legally obtained practical experience and 576 hours of related instruction/education.
Required four years licensed journeyman experience

plumbing.name: Master Plumber / Journeyman Plumber license
plumbing.covers: Anyone working in the field of plumbing as a master or journeyman.
prerequisites: Journeyman: 5 years of legally obtained plumbing experience or a completed approved apprenticeship
Pass the board exam
plumbing.summary: Plumbers must hold a state master or journeyman plumber license. Journeymen need 5 years of experience or a completed apprenticeship and must pass the board's exam.
plumbing.quote: a person working at the field of plumbing in this state, either as a master plumber or as a journeyman plumber, shall first obtain a license as provided in Title 37, chapter 69, part 3.
plumbing.note: Master plumber experience requirements were not checked.

evidence.quote: a specific record of 5 years of legally obtained experience in the field of plumbing. This experience requirement may be fulfilled by: (i) working 5 years in a major phase of the plumbing business
must at a time and place designated by the board be examined as to the qualifications for a license.

mechanical.agency: Montana DLI Building Codes Program / certified local governments
mechanical.covers: HVAC/mechanical work needs permits and inspections, but no state HVAC trade license was found.
prerequisites: Construction Contractor License (if you have employees or are a corporation/manager-managed LLC)
Mechanical permits from the state or certified local government
mechanical.summary: Montana does not appear to issue a state HVAC/mechanical trade license; mechanical work is controlled through permits from the state Building Codes Program or a certified local government. Gas piping and plumbing parts may need a licensed plumber.
mechanical.quote: Mechanical permit holders must call for gas piping pressure tests, rough-in and final inspections.
mechanical.note: No official page states outright that Montana has no HVAC license; based on the DLI list of licensing programs, which has no mechanical/HVAC board.

roofing.name: Construction Contractor License (CCL)
roofing.covers: The CCL definition expressly includes installing or repairing roofing or siding.
prerequisites: Workers' compensation and unemployment coverage for employees, or an ICEC if working alone
roofing.summary: There is no separate roofing license; roofers fall under the general Construction Contractor License (or an ICEC if working alone).
roofing.quote: including the installation of carpeting or other floor covering, the erection of scaffolding or other structures or works, or the installation or repair of roofing or siding

pesticide.name: Commercial Applicator license
pesticide.covers: Anyone in the business of applying pesticides (lawn, weed, tree and structural pest control).
prerequisites: Pass the required exams
Liability insurance (financial responsibility)
pesticide.insurance: Commercial applicators must carry liability insurance.
pesticide.summary: To apply pesticides as a business you need a Montana commercial applicator license, which requires passing exams and carrying liability insurance.
pesticide.quote: Any person in the business of applying pesticides must obtain an applicator's license from the department. To obtain a license, a person must pass examinations, complete an application form and pay a licensing fee.

evidence.quote: must meet financial liability requirements. These liability requirements may only be met through liability insurance.

asbestos.name: Asbestos occupation accreditation (contractor/supervisor, worker) and DEQ asbestos project permits
asbestos.agency: Montana Department of Environmental Quality, Asbestos Control Program
asbestos.covers: People working in asbestos-related occupations; asbestos projects require DEQ permits.
prerequisites: Approved asbestos training course
Pass a department-approved exam
DEQ project permit
asbestos.summary: Asbestos workers and contractors must be accredited by DEQ after approved training and an exam, and asbestos projects need a DEQ permit.
asbestos.quote: To qualify for accreditation in a particular asbestos-related occupation, a person must: (a) (i) successfully complete an asbestos-related training course for that occupation approved by the department or the United States environmental protection agency; and (ii) pass an examination approved by the department
asbestos.note: deq.mt.gov failed TLS verification with curl, so statutes were cited instead of the DEQ program page.

evidence.quote: The department shall review a permit application within 5 working days of receipt of a complete application and an appropriate fee for an asbestos project

lead_rrp.name: EPA Lead-Safe Certified Firm + Certified Renovator (federal)
lead_rrp.covers: Paid renovation, repair and painting that disturbs paint in pre-1978 homes, childcare facilities and preschools.
prerequisites: EPA firm certification
Certified renovator training
lead_rrp.summary: Montana is not on EPA's list of states running their own RRP program, so renovation firms are certified directly by EPA.
lead_rrp.quote: EPA administers the RRP Program in most Tribes, states and territories, but has authorized the following to operate their own programs: Alabama, Delaware, Georgia, Iowa, Kansas, Massachusetts, Mississippi, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Oregon, Rhode Island, Utah, Vermont, Washington, Wisconsin

evidence.quote: EPA's RRP Rule requires that anyone paid to perform work that disturbs painted surfaces in homes, childcare facilities and preschools built before 1978 be certified and their employees be trained

other.name: Independent Contractor Exemption Certificate (ICEC)
other.summary: Solo contractors without employees get an ICEC (no test) instead of workers' comp coverage.
other.quote: Covered under a self-elected workers' compensation insurance policy or obtain an Independent Contractor Exemption Certificate (ICEC).
